# External pointers

{{< include _setup.qmd >}}

An external pointer (`EXTPTRSXP`) wraps a C `void*` so it can be passed
through R code. R treats the pointer as opaque; you use it to manage C-side
resources (handles, connections, data structures) that outlive a single
`.Call`. Because R can't see what the pointer owns, you register a
finalizer to release the resource when the SEXP is garbage collected.

## Create and access

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
render_entries("external-pointers", "Create and access")
```

## Finalization

A finalizer has the signature:

```c
typedef void (*R_CFinalizer_t)(SEXP);
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
render_entries("external-pointers", "Finalization")
```

## Weak references

Weak references (`WEAKREFXP`) reference an object without keeping it alive;
they're used with finalizers to run code when an object is collected.

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
render_entries("external-pointers", "Weak references")
```
